layer1_nasaScienceDataPortalPolicy.rule: NASA-led data without restrictive notice/license = CC0; 'no restrictions on the usage'; a labeled licence, if provided, governs; media policy explicitly excluded from this scope

layer2_nasaEarthdataPolicy.rule: same CC0 default; content generally not copyrighted; use for Internet webpages within stated scope; sharing includes private industry; restricted/third-party content must be labelled, otherwise default applies

layer3_powerSpecificMetadata.rule: POWER = NASA LaRC Applied Sciences project over NASA sources (CERES, GMAO); project self-declares 'no restrictions on the use, access, and/or download'; the only licence label anywhere is CC BY 4.0 (permissive); NO restrictive notice found on any POWER official page (0 keyword hits, 2026-09-13 sweep)

layer4_powerAttributionRules.rule: citation of POWER + service name + version + access date = officially requested practice with fixed template; acknowledgement text provided; publication/redistribution notifications are requests, not permission requirements

layer5_utripaActualUse.rule: build-time fetch -> store -> normalize -> aggregate -> derived canonical -> commercial SSG display with attribution; no raw mirror, no bulk download to users, no endorsement, no NASA marks

rightsChain.chainVerdict: The five layers form a complete authorization chain. Two licence branches both authorize the usage: (A) CC0 default applies to unlabelled API-delivered POWER data -> 'even for commercial purposes ... without asking permission'; (B) the CC BY 4.0 label applies -> 'share and adapt for any purpose, even commercially' with attribution. Under either branch UTRIPLA's use is authorized; the ambiguity between branches is therefore non-blocking and is recorded only as a documentation caveat (which attribution wording to prefer).
